title: The Book of Isaiah
subtitle: Who each prophecy was spoken to, the great themes, and where its promises lead: to the return from Babylon, to Christ, and to the new creation
summary: Isaiah son of Amoz preached in Jerusalem for about forty years, from the year King Uzziah died (about 740 BC) into the reign of Hezekiah. His world was ruled by Assyria, which swallowed the northern kingdom of Israel in 722 BC and nearly took Jerusalem in 701. The book moves in three parts. Chapters 1–39 speak to Judah in Isaiah's own day: judgment on a proud and unjust people, and hope in a coming King. Chapters 40–55 speak comfort to the exiles in Babylon more than a century later: their God is the only God, he will send Cyrus to set them free, and his Servant will carry their sin. Chapters 56–66 speak to the people back home, still waiting, and end with new heavens and a new earth. Many scholars think later prophets in Isaiah's line wrote the second and third parts; Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament, which quotes both halves under Isaiah's name (John 12:38–41), receive the book as his. Either way it asks to be read as one: "the Holy One of Israel," Isaiah's own name for God, appears 12 times in chapters 1–39 and 14 times in chapters 40–66. Isaiah is the prophet the New Testament quotes most. Every passage here is tagged with who it was spoken to, when it comes true, and what kind of word it is, and linked to where the rest of the Bible picks it up.

views.title: The book in order
views.note: Eight movements, from the case against Judah to the new heavens and the new earth.

groups.title: The case against Judah (1–5)
groups.note: The book opens like a courtroom: God brings charges against his own people, and offers to wash them clean.

refs.label: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz
refs.note: Seen “during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah”: about 740 to 686 BC.

links.label: 2 Chronicles 26:22
links.note: Isaiah also wrote the acts of King Uzziah.

refs.label: “Come now, let us reason together”
refs.note: Heaven and earth are called as witnesses. God is sick of sacrifices offered by hands full of blood: “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow.”

links.label: Romans 9:29
links.note: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants” (1:9).

refs.label: The mountain of the LORD's house
refs.note: “In the last days” all nations stream to Zion to learn God's ways, and beat their swords into plowshares.

refs.label: The Branch of the LORD, and a people called holy
refs.note: After the judgment, the survivors left in Zion are washed clean and sheltered by the cloud and fire of the exodus.

refs.label: The song of the vineyard
refs.note: God planted Israel like a choice vine: “He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress.”

refs.label: Six woes
refs.note: Woe to those who add house to house, who call evil good and good evil, who are wise in their own eyes.

groups.title: The call, and the Immanuel book (6–12)
groups.note: Isaiah sees the King, and is sent to a people who will not listen. Then Assyria's shadow falls, and a child is promised.

refs.label: “Holy, holy, holy”: Isaiah's call
refs.note: In the year King Uzziah died Isaiah sees the Lord on his throne. A coal from the altar touches his lips: “Here am I. Send me!”

links.label: John 12:41
links.note: “Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus' glory and spoke about Him.”

refs.label: Ever hearing, never understanding
refs.note: Isaiah's message will harden a people who refuse it, until the land is emptied. Yet a stump is left: “the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”

refs.label: A sign for Ahaz: Immanuel
refs.note: About 734 BC Aram and Israel march on Jerusalem, and King Ahaz will not trust God. The sign: “the virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.” Before the boy is grown, both enemy kings will be gone.

links.label: Matthew 1:22–23
links.topic: Born of the virgin: God with us

links.label: 2 Kings 16:5–9
links.note: He sends the temple's silver and gold to Assyria, which takes Damascus and kills Rezin.

links.label: 2 Kings 15:29–30
links.note: Assyria takes Galilee, and Pekah of Israel is assassinated.

refs.label: A sanctuary, and a stone of stumbling
refs.note: Do not fear what this people fears. The LORD himself will be a sanctuary, and to both houses of Israel “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.”

refs.label: “Here am I, and the children the LORD has given me”
refs.note: Isaiah and his sons, whose names are messages, wait for the LORD while he hides his face.

links.label: Hebrews 2:13
links.topic: Spoken by Christ of his brothers

refs.label: “For unto us a child is born”
refs.note: Zebulun and Naphtali, the first land to fall to Assyria, will see a great light. The child will be called “Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace,” and reign on David's throne with no end.

links.label: Luke 1:32–33
links.topic: The throne of his father David

refs.label: Assyria, the rod of My anger
refs.note: God uses Assyria to discipline his people, then judges its pride: “Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it?”

refs.label: A remnant will return
refs.note: Isaiah's son was named Shear-jashub, “a remnant will return” (7:3). The survivors will rely on the LORD, “the Holy One of Israel.”

refs.label: A shoot from the stump of Jesse
refs.note: From David's cut-down family tree a Branch grows. The Spirit of the LORD rests on him; he judges the poor with justice; the wolf lives with the lamb; the nations seek him.

links.label: Romans 15:12
links.topic: The Root of Jesse, hope of the nations

links.label: Revelation 22:16
links.topic: “I am the Root and the Offspring of David”

refs.label: A second exodus
refs.note: “The Lord will extend His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people,” from Assyria, Egypt and the islands of the sea.

refs.label: Songs of salvation
refs.note: “With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.”

groups.title: Oracles against the nations (13–23)
groups.note: Burdens against every power around Judah. The point for Judah: do not trust them, and do not fear them. The LORD rules them all.

refs.label: Babylon: the day of the LORD
refs.note: Babylon, not yet the great power of the day, will fall to the Medes and be left a ruin.

links.label: Daniel 5:30–31
links.topic: Babylon falls to Darius the Mede, 539 BC

refs.label: “How you have fallen from heaven, O day star”
refs.note: A taunt over the king of Babylon, who said in his heart “I will ascend to the heavens.” Many readers have also heard in it the fall of Satan; Jesus uses its words of Capernaum.

refs.label: “I will break Assyria in My land”
refs.note: “As I have planned, so will it be.” Fulfilled when Assyria's army died outside Jerusalem.

refs.label: A throne in the tent of David
refs.note: Even inside the oracle against Moab: “in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David,” and a judge seeking justice will sit on it.

refs.label: Damascus a heap of ruins
refs.note: Aram's capital, Ahaz's enemy in chapter 7, “is no longer a city.”

refs.label: “Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork”
refs.note: The book's most surprising promise: Israel's two great enemies will worship the LORD together with her, joined by a highway. “Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance.”

refs.label: Isaiah walks barefoot
refs.note: For three years Isaiah goes stripped and barefoot as a sign that Egypt and Cush, the allies Judah was counting on, will be led away by Assyria.

refs.label: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon!”
refs.note: The watchman's cry over Babylon, heard again over the last Babylon in Revelation.

links.label: Revelation 14:8
links.topic: The same cry at the end

links.label: Revelation 18:2
links.topic: The same cry at the end

refs.label: The key to the house of David
refs.note: Proud steward Shebna is replaced by Eliakim: “What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.”

links.label: Revelation 3:7
links.topic: He who holds the key of David

groups.title: The whole earth, and the feast to come (24–35)
groups.note: The view widens to the whole world: the earth judged, death swallowed up, and warnings to Jerusalem's leaders who trust Egypt instead of God.

refs.label: The earth laid waste
refs.note: “The earth is defiled by its people; they have … broken the everlasting covenant.” The judgment is on the whole world.

refs.label: A feast for all peoples, and death swallowed up
refs.note: “On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet for all the peoples.” He will swallow up death forever and wipe away the tears from every face.

links.label: 1 Corinthians 15:54
links.topic: “Death has been swallowed up in victory”

refs.label: “Your dead will live; their bodies will rise”
refs.note: One of the Old Testament's clearest words of resurrection.

links.label: John 5:28–29
links.topic: All in the graves will hear his voice

refs.label: A cornerstone in Zion
refs.note: Jerusalem's rulers boast of a “covenant with death” (a treaty with Egypt). God lays in Zion a tested, precious cornerstone instead.

links.label: Romans 10:11
links.topic: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame”

refs.label: Honoring Me with their lips
refs.note: “Their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men.”

links.label: 1 Corinthians 1:19
links.topic: The wisdom of the wise destroyed

refs.label: “By repentance and rest you would be saved”
refs.note: Judah runs to Egypt for horses. “Your strength would lie in quiet confidence—but you were not willing.” Still, “the LORD longs to be gracious to you.”

refs.label: “A king will reign in righteousness”
refs.note: Each ruler will be like a shelter from the wind, and the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed.

refs.label: The desert will bloom
refs.note: “Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped. Then the lame will leap like a deer.” The ransomed return to Zion on a highway called the Way of Holiness.

links.label: Matthew 11:4–5
links.topic: “Report to John what you hear and see”

groups.title: Hezekiah: from Assyria to Babylon (36–39)
groups.note: The hinge of the book: Assyria is turned back from Jerusalem in 701 BC, and then Isaiah foretells Babylon. The rest of the book speaks into that exile.

refs.label: Sennacherib's threat and Hezekiah's prayer
refs.note: Assyria takes Judah's fortified cities and mocks the LORD at Jerusalem's wall. Hezekiah spreads the letter out before the LORD and prays.

refs.label: The LORD answers: Assyria turned back
refs.note: “He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it.” That night the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib goes home to Nineveh.

links.label: 2 Chronicles 32:20–22
links.topic: Hezekiah and Isaiah cried out to heaven

refs.label: Hezekiah healed: fifteen more years
refs.note: “I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears.”

refs.label: Babylon's envoys, and a word of exile
refs.note: Hezekiah shows the envoys from Babylon all his treasures. Everything in his palace, and some of his own descendants, will be carried off to Babylon.

links.label: Daniel 1:1–3
links.topic: Young men of the royal family taken to Babylon

groups.title: Comfort, My people (40–48)
groups.note: Now the voice speaks to exiles in Babylon: the punishment is over, their God is the only God, and he will bring them home through Cyrus.

refs.label: “Comfort, comfort My people”
refs.note: Her iniquity is pardoned. A voice calls: prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness. “The word of our God stands forever.” He tends his flock like a shepherd.

links.label: Luke 3:3–6
links.topic: John the Baptist, the voice in the wilderness

links.label: John 1:23
links.topic: “I am a voice of one calling”

refs.label: “To whom will you compare Me?”
refs.note: The Creator who measures the waters in his hand does not grow tired: “Those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles.”

links.label: Romans 11:34
links.topic: “Who has known the mind of the Lord?”

refs.label: “Israel, My servant … do not fear”
refs.note: “Do not fear, for I am with you.” Here the servant is Israel; later the Servant will be one person.

refs.label: “Here is My Servant”: the first Servant song
refs.note: Chosen, upheld, filled with the Spirit, he brings justice to the nations gently: “A bruised reed He will not break.” A light to the nations, opening blind eyes.

links.label: Matthew 3:17
links.topic: “In whom I am well pleased” at his baptism

refs.label: “When you pass through the waters”
refs.note: “I have called you by your name; you are Mine!”

refs.label: “I am about to do something new”
refs.note: The God who made a path through the sea will make a way in the wilderness: a new exodus, from Babylon.

refs.label: “I am the first and I am the last”
refs.note: There is no God but the LORD. Then a biting satire: a man burns half a log to roast his meat, and from the rest makes a god and bows down to it.

links.label: Revelation 1:17
links.topic: Jesus: “I am the First and the Last”

refs.label: Cyrus, My shepherd
refs.note: The LORD names Cyrus of Persia, “His anointed,” who will say of Jerusalem “She will be rebuilt.” Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BC and sent the exiles home.

links.label: Ezra 1:1–4
links.topic: Cyrus's decree to rebuild the temple
links.note: Ezra credits the timing to Jeremiah's word; the decree does what Isaiah 44:28 said Cyrus would do.

links.label: 2 Chronicles 36:22–23
links.topic: The last words of the Hebrew Bible

refs.label: “Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth”
refs.note: “Every knee will bow before Me, every tongue will swear allegiance.”

links.label: Philippians 2:9–11
links.topic: Every knee bows at the name of Jesus

links.label: Romans 14:10–12
links.topic: Every tongue will confess to God

refs.label: “I declare the end from the beginning”
refs.note: The idols have to be carried; the LORD carries his people, and his purpose will stand.

refs.label: Babylon brought down
refs.note: The proud city who said “I will be queen forever … I am, and there is none besides me” will lose everything in a single day.

links.label: Daniel 5:25–31
links.topic: The writing on the wall, 539 BC

links.label: Revelation 18:7–8
links.topic: “I sit as queen”: the last Babylon

refs.label: “Leave Babylon!”
refs.note: “Declare it with a shout of joy … The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!” And a warning: “There is no peace,” says the LORD, “for the wicked.”

links.label: Ezra 1:5
links.topic: The exiles go up to rebuild

groups.title: The Servant and the new exodus (49–55)
groups.note: The Servant who will do what Israel could not: bring the nations light, and carry the sin of many. Then an open invitation to everyone who is thirsty.

refs.label: A light for the nations: the second Servant song
refs.note: “It is not enough for You to be My Servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob … I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth.”

links.label: Acts 13:46–47
links.topic: Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles

refs.label: “Can a woman forget her nursing child?”
refs.note: “Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!” The day of salvation, and a people led beside springs of water.

refs.label: “I offered My back to those who struck Me”: the third Servant song
refs.note: Taught by God morning by morning, the Servant does not hide his face from scorn and spittle, and sets his face like flint.

links.label: Matthew 26:67–68
links.topic: They spit in his face and struck him

links.label: Luke 9:51
links.topic: He resolutely set out for Jerusalem

refs.label: “Awake, awake, O arm of the LORD”
refs.note: The arm that dried up the sea will bring the redeemed home: “sorrow and sighing will flee.”

refs.label: “How beautiful on the mountains”
refs.note: The messenger runs to Zion with good news: “Your God reigns!”

links.label: Romans 10:14–15
links.topic: Sent to preach the good news

refs.label: The suffering Servant: the fourth Servant song
refs.note: Despised and rejected, “pierced for our transgressions … crushed for our iniquities,” silent like a lamb led to the slaughter. “The LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.” After his suffering he will see the light of life and justify many.

links.label: Acts 8:30–35
links.topic: Philip tells the eunuch who it is about

links.label: Matthew 27:57–60
links.topic: With a rich man in his death

links.label: Hebrews 9:28
links.topic: Offered once to bear the sins of many

refs.label: “Shout for joy, O barren woman”
refs.note: The deserted wife will have more children than ever: “My loving devotion will not depart from you.”

refs.label: “Come, all you who are thirsty”
refs.note: Buy wine and milk without money. An everlasting covenant, “My loving devotion promised to David.” “My thoughts are not your thoughts,” and the word that will not return empty.

links.label: Acts 13:34
links.topic: The sure blessings of David, in the risen Jesus

links.label: John 7:37–38
links.topic: “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me”

links.label: Revelation 22:17
links.topic: “Let the one who is thirsty come”

groups.title: Your light has come (56–66)
groups.note: Back from exile, the people wait, fast, and fail again. God promises his own arm will save, a Spirit-anointed messenger, and at last new heavens and a new earth.

refs.label: A house of prayer for all the nations
refs.note: Foreigners and eunuchs who hold fast to God's covenant are welcomed: “My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.”

links.label: Acts 8:35–39
links.note: He was reading Isaiah 53 when Philip met him.

refs.label: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the humble”
refs.note: The One “whose name is Holy” lives with the lowly to revive them. But “there is no peace,” says my God, “for the wicked.”

refs.label: The fast I have chosen
refs.note: They fast while they quarrel and exploit their workers. The fast God wants: “to set the oppressed free … to share your bread with the hungry.” Then “your light will break forth like the dawn.”

links.label: Luke 4:18
links.topic: Jesus joins “release the oppressed” to Isaiah 61

refs.label: Sin's barrier, and the Redeemer who comes
refs.note: “Your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God.” No one intervenes, so the LORD puts on righteousness like a breastplate and salvation like a helmet: “The Redeemer will come to Zion.”

refs.label: “Arise, shine, for your light has come”
refs.note: Nations come to the light, bringing gold and frankincense. “The LORD will be your everlasting light.”

links.label: Matthew 2:11
links.topic: Gold and frankincense for the child

refs.label: “The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me”
refs.note: Good news to the poor, liberty to the captives, “the year of the LORD's favor and the day of our God's vengeance.” In Nazareth Jesus read it and stopped before the day of vengeance: “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

links.label: Matthew 5:3–4
links.topic: Blessed are the poor and those who mourn

refs.label: A new name
refs.note: No longer “Forsaken” or “Desolate”: “as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.”

links.label: Revelation 21:2
links.topic: A bride adorned for her husband

refs.label: The one who treads the winepress
refs.note: A warrior comes from Edom with garments stained red: “I have trodden the winepress alone.”

refs.label: “If only You would rend the heavens and come down”
refs.note: “All our righteous acts are like filthy rags … we are the clay, and You are the potter.” No eye has seen any God but this one, “who acts on behalf of those who wait for Him.”

links.label: Mark 1:10
links.topic: The heavens torn open at his baptism

refs.label: New heavens and a new earth
refs.note: The former things forgotten, no more weeping, and “the wolf and the lamb will feed together.”

refs.label: “Heaven is My throne”
refs.note: No house can hold him. “This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.”

refs.label: All nations will see My glory
refs.note: God gathers all nations and tongues, sends messengers to far coasts, and chooses priests and Levites from those he gathers. The book ends with the new heavens and earth, and a stark warning.

links.label: Romans 15:16
links.topic: The nations as an offering to God

links.label: Philippians 2:9–11
links.topic: Every knee bows at the name of Jesus

refs.label: A light for the nations: the second Servant song
refs.note: “It is not enough for You to be My Servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob … I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth.”

refs.label: “I offered My back to those who struck Me”: the third Servant song
refs.note: Taught by God morning by morning, the Servant does not hide his face from scorn and spittle, and sets his face like flint.

links.label: Matthew 26:67–68
links.topic: They spit in his face and struck him

links.label: Luke 9:51
links.topic: He resolutely set out for Jerusalem

refs.label: The suffering Servant: the fourth Servant song
refs.note: Despised and rejected, “pierced for our transgressions … crushed for our iniquities,” silent like a lamb led to the slaughter. “The LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.” After his suffering he will see the light of life and justify many.

links.label: Acts 8:30–35
links.topic: Philip tells the eunuch who it is about

links.label: Matthew 27:57–60
links.topic: With a rich man in his death

refs.label: “Come, all you who are thirsty”
refs.note: Buy wine and milk without money. An everlasting covenant, “My loving devotion promised to David.” “My thoughts are not your thoughts,” and the word that will not return empty.

links.label: Acts 13:34
links.topic: The sure blessings of David, in the risen Jesus

refs.label: “Arise, shine, for your light has come”
refs.note: Nations come to the light, bringing gold and frankincense. “The LORD will be your everlasting light.”

links.label: Matthew 2:11
links.topic: Gold and frankincense for the child

refs.label: “If only You would rend the heavens and come down”
refs.note: “All our righteous acts are like filthy rags … we are the clay, and You are the potter.” No eye has seen any God but this one, “who acts on behalf of those who wait for Him.”

links.label: Mark 1:10
links.topic: The heavens torn open at his baptism

refs.label: The song of the vineyard
refs.note: God planted Israel like a choice vine: “He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress.”

refs.label: Ever hearing, never understanding
refs.note: Isaiah's message will harden a people who refuse it, until the land is emptied. Yet a stump is left: “the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”

refs.label: A shoot from the stump of Jesse
refs.note: From David's cut-down family tree a Branch grows. The Spirit of the LORD rests on him; he judges the poor with justice; the wolf lives with the lamb; the nations seek him.

links.label: Revelation 22:16
links.topic: “I am the Root and the Offspring of David”

refs.label: “How you have fallen from heaven, O day star”
refs.note: A taunt over the king of Babylon, who said in his heart “I will ascend to the heavens.” Many readers have also heard in it the fall of Satan; Jesus uses its words of Capernaum.

refs.label: A feast for all peoples, and death swallowed up
refs.note: “On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet for all the peoples.” He will swallow up death forever and wipe away the tears from every face.

refs.label: “Your dead will live; their bodies will rise”
refs.note: One of the Old Testament's clearest words of resurrection.

links.label: John 5:28–29
links.topic: All in the graves will hear his voice

refs.label: Honoring Me with their lips
refs.note: “Their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men.”

refs.label: The desert will bloom
refs.note: “Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped. Then the lame will leap like a deer.” The ransomed return to Zion on a highway called the Way of Holiness.

links.label: Matthew 11:4–5
links.topic: “Report to John what you hear and see”

refs.label: “I am the first and I am the last”
refs.note: There is no God but the LORD. Then a biting satire: a man burns half a log to roast his meat, and from the rest makes a god and bows down to it.

links.label: Revelation 1:17
links.topic: Jesus: “I am the First and the Last”

refs.label: The suffering Servant: the fourth Servant song
refs.note: Despised and rejected, “pierced for our transgressions … crushed for our iniquities,” silent like a lamb led to the slaughter. “The LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.” After his suffering he will see the light of life and justify many.

refs.label: “Come, all you who are thirsty”
refs.note: Buy wine and milk without money. An everlasting covenant, “My loving devotion promised to David.” “My thoughts are not your thoughts,” and the word that will not return empty.

links.label: John 7:37–38
links.topic: “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me”

refs.label: A house of prayer for all the nations
refs.note: Foreigners and eunuchs who hold fast to God's covenant are welcomed: “My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.”

refs.label: The fast I have chosen
refs.note: They fast while they quarrel and exploit their workers. The fast God wants: “to set the oppressed free … to share your bread with the hungry.” Then “your light will break forth like the dawn.”

links.label: Luke 4:18
links.topic: Jesus joins “release the oppressed” to Isaiah 61

refs.label: “The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me”
refs.note: Good news to the poor, liberty to the captives, “the year of the LORD's favor and the day of our God's vengeance.” In Nazareth Jesus read it and stopped before the day of vengeance: “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

links.label: Matthew 5:3–4
links.topic: Blessed are the poor and those who mourn

refs.label: All nations will see My glory
refs.note: God gathers all nations and tongues, sends messengers to far coasts, and chooses priests and Levites from those he gathers. The book ends with the new heavens and earth, and a stark warning.

refs.label: “Come now, let us reason together”
refs.note: Heaven and earth are called as witnesses. God is sick of sacrifices offered by hands full of blood: “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow.”

links.label: Romans 9:29
links.note: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants” (1:9).

refs.label: Ever hearing, never understanding
refs.note: Isaiah's message will harden a people who refuse it, until the land is emptied. Yet a stump is left: “the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”

refs.label: A remnant will return
refs.note: Isaiah's son was named Shear-jashub, “a remnant will return” (7:3). The survivors will rely on the LORD, “the Holy One of Israel.”

refs.label: A cornerstone in Zion
refs.note: Jerusalem's rulers boast of a “covenant with death” (a treaty with Egypt). God lays in Zion a tested, precious cornerstone instead.

links.label: Romans 10:11
links.topic: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame”

refs.label: Honoring Me with their lips
refs.note: “Their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men.”

links.label: 1 Corinthians 1:19
links.topic: The wisdom of the wise destroyed

refs.label: The desert will bloom
refs.note: “Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped. Then the lame will leap like a deer.” The ransomed return to Zion on a highway called the Way of Holiness.

refs.label: “Comfort, comfort My people”
refs.note: Her iniquity is pardoned. A voice calls: prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness. “The word of our God stands forever.” He tends his flock like a shepherd.

refs.label: “To whom will you compare Me?”
refs.note: The Creator who measures the waters in his hand does not grow tired: “Those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles.”

links.label: Romans 11:34
links.topic: “Who has known the mind of the Lord?”

refs.label: “Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth”
refs.note: “Every knee will bow before Me, every tongue will swear allegiance.”

links.label: Romans 14:10–12
links.topic: Every tongue will confess to God

refs.label: A light for the nations: the second Servant song
refs.note: “It is not enough for You to be My Servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob … I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth.”

links.label: Acts 13:46–47
links.topic: Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles

refs.label: “Can a woman forget her nursing child?”
refs.note: “Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!” The day of salvation, and a people led beside springs of water.

refs.label: “I offered My back to those who struck Me”: the third Servant song
refs.note: Taught by God morning by morning, the Servant does not hide his face from scorn and spittle, and sets his face like flint.

refs.label: “How beautiful on the mountains”
refs.note: The messenger runs to Zion with good news: “Your God reigns!”

links.label: Romans 10:14–15
links.topic: Sent to preach the good news

refs.label: The suffering Servant: the fourth Servant song
refs.note: Despised and rejected, “pierced for our transgressions … crushed for our iniquities,” silent like a lamb led to the slaughter. “The LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.” After his suffering he will see the light of life and justify many.

links.label: Hebrews 9:28
links.topic: Offered once to bear the sins of many

refs.label: “Shout for joy, O barren woman”
refs.note: The deserted wife will have more children than ever: “My loving devotion will not depart from you.”

refs.label: A house of prayer for all the nations
refs.note: Foreigners and eunuchs who hold fast to God's covenant are welcomed: “My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.”

links.label: Acts 8:35–39
links.note: He was reading Isaiah 53 when Philip met him.

refs.label: Sin's barrier, and the Redeemer who comes
refs.note: “Your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God.” No one intervenes, so the LORD puts on righteousness like a breastplate and salvation like a helmet: “The Redeemer will come to Zion.”

refs.label: “If only You would rend the heavens and come down”
refs.note: “All our righteous acts are like filthy rags … we are the clay, and You are the potter.” No eye has seen any God but this one, “who acts on behalf of those who wait for Him.”

refs.label: “Heaven is My throne”
refs.note: No house can hold him. “This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.”

refs.label: All nations will see My glory
refs.note: God gathers all nations and tongues, sends messengers to far coasts, and chooses priests and Levites from those he gathers. The book ends with the new heavens and earth, and a stark warning.

links.label: Romans 15:16
links.topic: The nations as an offering to God

refs.label: “Holy, holy, holy”: Isaiah's call
refs.note: In the year King Uzziah died Isaiah sees the Lord on his throne. A coal from the altar touches his lips: “Here am I. Send me!”

refs.label: A shoot from the stump of Jesse
refs.note: From David's cut-down family tree a Branch grows. The Spirit of the LORD rests on him; he judges the poor with justice; the wolf lives with the lamb; the nations seek him.

refs.label: “Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork”
refs.note: The book's most surprising promise: Israel's two great enemies will worship the LORD together with her, joined by a highway. “Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance.”

refs.label: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon!”
refs.note: The watchman's cry over Babylon, heard again over the last Babylon in Revelation.

links.label: Revelation 14:8
links.topic: The same cry at the end

links.label: Revelation 18:2
links.topic: The same cry at the end

refs.label: A feast for all peoples, and death swallowed up
refs.note: “On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet for all the peoples.” He will swallow up death forever and wipe away the tears from every face.

links.label: 1 Corinthians 15:54
links.topic: “Death has been swallowed up in victory”

refs.label: Babylon brought down
refs.note: The proud city who said “I will be queen forever … I am, and there is none besides me” will lose everything in a single day.

links.label: Revelation 18:7–8
links.topic: “I sit as queen”: the last Babylon

refs.label: “Leave Babylon!”
refs.note: “Declare it with a shout of joy … The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!” And a warning: “There is no peace,” says the LORD, “for the wicked.”

refs.label: “Can a woman forget her nursing child?”
refs.note: “Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!” The day of salvation, and a people led beside springs of water.

refs.label: “Come, all you who are thirsty”
refs.note: Buy wine and milk without money. An everlasting covenant, “My loving devotion promised to David.” “My thoughts are not your thoughts,” and the word that will not return empty.

links.label: Revelation 22:17
links.topic: “Let the one who is thirsty come”

refs.label: Sin's barrier, and the Redeemer who comes
refs.note: “Your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God.” No one intervenes, so the LORD puts on righteousness like a breastplate and salvation like a helmet: “The Redeemer will come to Zion.”

refs.label: “Arise, shine, for your light has come”
refs.note: Nations come to the light, bringing gold and frankincense. “The LORD will be your everlasting light.”

refs.label: A new name
refs.note: No longer “Forsaken” or “Desolate”: “as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.”

links.label: Revelation 21:2
links.topic: A bride adorned for her husband

refs.label: The one who treads the winepress
refs.note: A warrior comes from Edom with garments stained red: “I have trodden the winepress alone.”

refs.label: New heavens and a new earth
refs.note: The former things forgotten, no more weeping, and “the wolf and the lamb will feed together.”

refs.label: A sign for Ahaz: Immanuel
refs.note: About 734 BC Aram and Israel march on Jerusalem, and King Ahaz will not trust God. The sign: “the virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.” Before the boy is grown, both enemy kings will be gone.

links.label: 2 Kings 15:29–30
links.note: Assyria takes Galilee, and Pekah of Israel is assassinated.

refs.label: Assyria, the rod of My anger
refs.note: God uses Assyria to discipline his people, then judges its pride: “Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it?”

refs.label: Babylon: the day of the LORD
refs.note: Babylon, not yet the great power of the day, will fall to the Medes and be left a ruin.

links.label: Daniel 5:30–31
links.topic: Babylon falls to Darius the Mede, 539 BC

refs.label: “I will break Assyria in My land”
refs.note: “As I have planned, so will it be.” Fulfilled when Assyria's army died outside Jerusalem.

refs.label: Damascus a heap of ruins
refs.note: Aram's capital, Ahaz's enemy in chapter 7, “is no longer a city.”

refs.label: Babylon's envoys, and a word of exile
refs.note: Hezekiah shows the envoys from Babylon all his treasures. Everything in his palace, and some of his own descendants, will be carried off to Babylon.

links.label: Daniel 1:1–3
links.topic: Young men of the royal family taken to Babylon

refs.label: Cyrus, My shepherd
refs.note: The LORD names Cyrus of Persia, “His anointed,” who will say of Jerusalem “She will be rebuilt.” Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BC and sent the exiles home.

links.label: Ezra 1:1–4
links.topic: Cyrus's decree to rebuild the temple
links.note: Ezra credits the timing to Jeremiah's word; the decree does what Isaiah 44:28 said Cyrus would do.

links.label: 2 Chronicles 36:22–23
links.topic: The last words of the Hebrew Bible

refs.label: Babylon brought down
refs.note: The proud city who said “I will be queen forever … I am, and there is none besides me” will lose everything in a single day.

links.label: Daniel 5:25–31
links.topic: The writing on the wall, 539 BC

refs.label: “Leave Babylon!”
refs.note: “Declare it with a shout of joy … The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!” And a warning: “There is no peace,” says the LORD, “for the wicked.”

links.label: Ezra 1:5
links.topic: The exiles go up to rebuild

groups.title: The same events in the histories

refs.label: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz
refs.note: Seen “during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah”: about 740 to 686 BC.

links.label: 2 Chronicles 26:22
links.note: Isaiah also wrote the acts of King Uzziah.

refs.label: A sign for Ahaz: Immanuel
refs.note: About 734 BC Aram and Israel march on Jerusalem, and King Ahaz will not trust God. The sign: “the virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.” Before the boy is grown, both enemy kings will be gone.

links.label: 2 Kings 16:5–9
links.note: He sends the temple's silver and gold to Assyria, which takes Damascus and kills Rezin.

refs.label: Sennacherib's threat and Hezekiah's prayer
refs.note: Assyria takes Judah's fortified cities and mocks the LORD at Jerusalem's wall. Hezekiah spreads the letter out before the LORD and prays.

refs.label: The LORD answers: Assyria turned back
refs.note: “He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it.” That night the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib goes home to Nineveh.

links.label: 2 Chronicles 32:20–22
links.topic: Hezekiah and Isaiah cried out to heaven

refs.label: The mountain of the LORD's house
refs.note: “In the last days” all nations stream to Zion to learn God's ways, and beat their swords into plowshares.

refs.label: The Branch of the LORD, and a people called holy
refs.note: After the judgment, the survivors left in Zion are washed clean and sheltered by the cloud and fire of the exodus.

refs.label: Six woes
refs.note: Woe to those who add house to house, who call evil good and good evil, who are wise in their own eyes.

refs.label: A second exodus
refs.note: “The Lord will extend His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people,” from Assyria, Egypt and the islands of the sea.

refs.label: Songs of salvation
refs.note: “With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.”

refs.label: A throne in the tent of David
refs.note: Even inside the oracle against Moab: “in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David,” and a judge seeking justice will sit on it.

refs.label: Isaiah walks barefoot
refs.note: For three years Isaiah goes stripped and barefoot as a sign that Egypt and Cush, the allies Judah was counting on, will be led away by Assyria.

refs.label: The earth laid waste
refs.note: “The earth is defiled by its people; they have … broken the everlasting covenant.” The judgment is on the whole world.

refs.label: “By repentance and rest you would be saved”
refs.note: Judah runs to Egypt for horses. “Your strength would lie in quiet confidence—but you were not willing.” Still, “the LORD longs to be gracious to you.”

refs.label: “A king will reign in righteousness”
refs.note: Each ruler will be like a shelter from the wind, and the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed.

refs.label: Hezekiah healed: fifteen more years
refs.note: “I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears.”

refs.label: “Israel, My servant … do not fear”
refs.note: “Do not fear, for I am with you.” Here the servant is Israel; later the Servant will be one person.

refs.label: “When you pass through the waters”
refs.note: “I have called you by your name; you are Mine!”

refs.label: “I am about to do something new”
refs.note: The God who made a path through the sea will make a way in the wilderness: a new exodus, from Babylon.

refs.label: “I declare the end from the beginning”
refs.note: The idols have to be carried; the LORD carries his people, and his purpose will stand.

refs.label: “Awake, awake, O arm of the LORD”
refs.note: The arm that dried up the sea will bring the redeemed home: “sorrow and sighing will flee.”

refs.label: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the humble”
refs.note: The One “whose name is Holy” lives with the lowly to revive them. But “there is no peace,” says my God, “for the wicked.”
